stories.headline: Council to oppose asylum seeker housing plan in Fenland village
stories.brief: Local authorities have announced they will robustly challenge a proposal to accommodate 26 asylum seekers within a Fenland village. The council confirmed its intention to fight the plans, though further details regarding the specific location or the timeline for the development have not been disclosed. Residents are advised to monitor official council updates as the situation progresses.

stories.headline: Police appeal to locate wanted man last seen in Wisbech
stories.brief:
Lincolnshire Police are asking for the public's help to find 34-year-old Davy Hill. He is wanted by officers in connection with an investigation into a rape. Mr Hill was last seen in the Wisbech area, though police believe he may have since travelled elsewhere.

Anyone with information regarding his current whereabouts is urged to contact the police. You can email wanted@lincs.police.uk, quoting reference 26000480721. Alternatively, you can call 101 or report details anonymously through the independent charity Crimestoppers.

stories.headline: Fleetwood Town Under-21s secure win in Peterborough
stories.brief: Fleetwood Town’s Under-21 side has claimed a victory following a match in Peterborough. The result was decided by a goal from Sawkins, who secured the win for the visiting team.

stories.headline: Ten Cambridgeshire pubs recognised for real ale
stories.brief: Ten pubs across Cambridgeshire have been named among the best venues for real ale in the United Kingdom. The recognition comes from the Ely Standard, which highlighted the local establishments for their quality offerings. The list celebrates the top spots for ale enthusiasts within the county.

stories.headline: New Best Start Family Hubs open across Cambridgeshire
stories.brief:
Cambridgeshire County Council has launched five new Best Start Family Hubs, including a site in Wisbech. These centres replace existing child and family facilities, bringing services like health, childcare, housing, and financial advice under one roof. While currently focused on support from pregnancy to age five, the service will eventually expand to assist young people up to age 19, or 25 for those with special educational needs.

The hubs are free to use and open to all families. Launch events are being held at each location throughout this week, offering residents the chance to meet staff and explore the available resources. Further information is also accessible through the council’s network of local sites and online services.

stories.headline: West Norfolk woman completes Ben Nevis climb for hospital unit
stories.brief:
A West Norfolk woman has raised over £540 for the Peddars Way end-of-life unit at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. Jan Mick climbed Ben Nevis in memory of her father, Harry, who passed away earlier this month. 

The challenge took nine hours and 20 minutes to complete, with Jan facing difficult conditions including strong winds, rain, and temperatures dropping to minus four degrees at the summit. Jan, who recently moved to the area from Hertfordshire, chose the climb to honour her father’s active lifestyle. The hospital has expressed its gratitude for the donation, which exceeded the original £200 target. Supporters can still contribute to the fundraiser online.

stories.headline: Government minister apologises for Whittlesey correspondence delay
stories.brief: A government minister has issued an apology after failing to respond to correspondence regarding the discovery of dead fish in Whittlesey. The issue, which was reported by the BBC, centres on a lack of communication from the minister’s office concerning the environmental incident. No further details regarding the cause of the fish deaths or the specific timeline of the correspondence have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: Fleetwood Town player looks ahead to Peterborough match
stories.brief: Fleetwood Town footballer Costelloe is preparing for the upcoming trip to Peterborough. Following his recent first-team debut, the player has expressed his desire to build on that performance as the squad heads into the fixture.

stories.headline: Plans proposed for two new wind farms in the Fens
stories.brief: Proposals have been submitted for the construction of two new wind farms in the region. The sites earmarked for the potential developments are located near Chatteris and Shippea Hill. No further details regarding the scale or timeline of these projects have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: Norfolk health officials consider future of A&E services
stories.brief:
Health officials in Norfolk are considering plans that could see A&E units at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn and the James Paget Hospital in Gorleston closed. Confidential documents reveal three potential options for future emergency care, with only one retaining full A&E services at all three of the county’s hospitals. Other proposals include downgrading the units to urgent treatment centres or removing major trauma services.

The Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group states that no final decisions have been made and that the documents are part of preliminary work. However, local MPs have expressed strong opposition to any potential downgrades, citing concerns over rural travel times and the impact on patient care.

stories.headline: Wisbech newsagent TG Jones to close in January
stories.brief:
The newsagent and stationer TG Jones has confirmed it will shut its Wisbech branch early next year. The shop, located on the Market Place, is scheduled to close its doors on Saturday, January 9, 2027. The closure is part of a wider, court-approved restructuring plan affecting several of the company's stores across the UK. 

A spokesperson for the retailer expressed regret over the impact on the local community and staff. A closing down sale will be held at the premises before the final closure date. The company stated that its current priority is supporting affected employees while continuing to serve customers during the final weeks of operation.

stories.headline: Three-year driving ban for holidaymaker caught in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
A holidaymaker has been disqualified from driving for three years after being caught over the limit in King’s Lynn. Forty-two-year-old David Canatch, from Gainsborough, was stopped by police on Gayton Road after officers noticed his fog lights were on during clear weather. A breath test revealed he had 45 micrograms of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath, exceeding the legal limit of 35.

Appearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Mr Canatch pleaded guilty to drink-driving. In addition to the driving ban, he was ordered to pay a £120 fine, a £48 victim surcharge, and £50 in court costs.

stories.headline: Free AI training pilot launched for Cambridge and Peterborough organisations
stories.brief: Organisations across the Cambridge and Peterborough area are being offered the chance to take part in a new artificial intelligence training pilot. The scheme, coordinated by the Cambridge Network, provides training sessions at no cost to participants. The initiative aims to support local groups and businesses looking to develop their understanding of AI technology. Further details regarding the programme and how to register for the pilot are available through the Cambridge Network.

stories.headline: Bus routes cut in Cambridgeshire village despite new shelters
stories.brief: A Cambridgeshire village has seen its bus services withdrawn, despite the recent installation of new bus shelters. The infrastructure project, which cost 16,000 pounds, was completed before the decision to cut the local routes was made. Residents in the area are now facing a loss of public transport links despite the significant investment in the facilities.

stories.headline: Candidates confirmed for Long Sutton by-election
stories.brief: The list of candidates standing in the upcoming by-election for Long Sutton has been officially announced. Residents in the area will head to the polls to select a new representative following the vacancy. Further details regarding the candidates and the polling process are expected to be made available to the public ahead of the vote.

stories.headline: Emergency lock closures leave boaters stranded in March
stories.brief: Boaters are currently unable to move through March following the announcement of emergency lock closures. The restrictions have left vessels marooned in the area. No further details regarding the cause of the closures or a timeline for the reopening of the waterway have been provided at this stage. Those planning to travel through the town by boat are advised to be aware of the disruption.

stories.headline: Opposition grows to Leverington asylum accommodation plans
stories.brief:
Fenland District Council and North East Cambridgeshire MP Steve Barclay have voiced strong opposition to government plans for a 26-bed asylum seeker facility in Leverington. The Home Office proposal for Roman Court is intended to house mothers and babies as part of a wider move toward long-term dispersal accommodation. 

However, local leaders have raised concerns regarding the suitability of the site and the potential for future changes to the facility's use. Mr Barclay has expressed fears that this is the first stage of a broader government policy to bring 205 asylum seekers into the district. No specific timeline for the project has been provided by the Home Office, which says it will continue to engage with local partners.

stories.headline: Improvement work begins at North Lynn ponds
stories.brief:
Maintenance work is starting today at the Loke Road ponds in North Lynn. West Norfolk Council staff are clearing overhanging and diseased trees to improve the habitat for local fish and invertebrates. The project involves cutting back willow trees and removing two ash trees identified as diseased. 

Officials say the work is necessary to prevent rotting leaves from depleting oxygen levels in the water and to reduce excessive shade. The clearance also aims to protect pond liners and dams from damage caused by aggressive willow roots. This initiative is part of a wider pond regeneration programme that began in 2023.

stories.headline: Wisbech fish and chip shop earns national recognition
stories.brief:
A Wisbech takeaway has been named among the best in the country. The Jolly Fryer, located on North End, has secured a place in the top 100 of a new national ranking. The list is compiled by the Fish & Chips app, which evaluates over 3,000 businesses across the UK. 

The rankings are updated monthly and are based on weighted scores from Google and Tripadvisor reviews. According to the app developers, shops cannot pay for inclusion, and the scoring system prioritises establishments with a higher volume of customer feedback.

stories.headline: New quantum eye imaging technology developed for children
stories.brief: Researchers at University College London and the company Siloton have collaborated to adapt quantum-enabled imaging technology specifically for use with children. The project aims to refine eye scanning techniques to better suit younger patients. Further details regarding the implementation or availability of this new diagnostic tool have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Health study results due for Whittlesey pit site
stories.brief: Findings from a health study concerning the controversial pit site in Whittlesey are set to be released. The report, which has been highlighted by the Cambs Times, examines the site that has previously been a subject of local debate. Further details regarding the study's conclusions are expected to be made public soon.

stories.headline: Developer reduces funding pledge for Fenland services
stories.brief: A property developer has withdrawn a fifty-thousand-pound commitment intended to support local services. The pledge was originally made to Fenland District Council. Reports suggest the move has drawn criticism regarding the council's oversight of such agreements. No further details have been provided regarding which specific services will be affected by the loss of this funding or how the council intends to respond to the developer's decision.

stories.headline: Wisbech High Street redevelopment plans approved
stories.brief:
Fenland District Council has approved plans to redevelop a vacant site on Wisbech High Street. The project will see the construction of commercial premises and six one-bedroom flats at numbers 11 and 12, with access provided via Castle Mews. The site has remained empty since the original Grade II listed buildings were demolished in 2020.

During a meeting on Wednesday, September 23, councillors described the two-decade delay in bringing the site back into use as embarrassing. Council leader Chris Boden has called for an explanation regarding previous administrative issues that stalled the development. Local representatives have welcomed the decision, noting that the project is a positive step for the town.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn sleep out raises over £7,000 for local night shelter
stories.brief:
A charity sleep out in King’s Lynn has raised more than £7,000 to support the town’s night shelter. Around 30 people spent Friday night in the grounds of the Minster to experience the challenges of sleeping rough. The funds will help the shelter, which relies entirely on community support and grants, as it prepares to reopen its doors on October 8.

The shelter is now appealing for food donations, including tinned goods, breakfast items, and long-life milk, to stock its cupboards for the winter season. Anyone interested in volunteering or donating can find further information on the King’s Lynn Night Shelter website or by calling 01553 776109.

stories.headline: Peterborough walkway project costs rise following skeleton discovery
stories.brief: The budget for a new walkway in Peterborough has increased by 1.6 million pounds. This additional expenditure follows the discovery of a skeleton at the construction site. The project, which aims to improve pedestrian access in the area, now faces higher costs due to the archaeological find. Further details regarding the impact on the construction timeline have not been released.

stories.headline: Conservative Party begins candidate selection for two Cambridgeshire seats
stories.brief: The Conservative Party has officially opened the process to select candidates for two parliamentary seats in Cambridgeshire. According to reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, the party is now accepting applications for these constituencies. Further details regarding the specific locations or the timeline for these selections have not yet been released. Residents interested in local political developments are advised to monitor official party announcements for updates as the selection process moves forward.

stories.headline: Financial loss expected for March bank site project
stories.brief: Fenland District Council is facing a projected loss of eight hundred thousand pounds regarding the regeneration of a bank site in March. Reports indicate the local authority expects the shortfall as work progresses on the development. No further details regarding the specific site or the reasons for the deficit have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: Wisbech academy hosts talks on the future of Fenland soil
stories.brief:
The Green Skills Academy in Wisbech has hosted a collaborative session focused on the future of agriculture and peat soil in the Fens. The event brought together the Fenland Environmental Network and the non-profit group Fenland SOIL to discuss the long-term sustainability of the local landscape. 

Organisers say the meeting provided a space for education providers and environmental groups to share expertise on land use and food production. The session aligns with the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Local Skills Improvement Plan, which highlights sustainable land management as a priority for the region. The College of West Anglia says the initiative aims to help students gain the skills needed to support the local economy’s shift toward a more sustainable future.

stories.headline: MP calls for Ely Junction upgrades to improve Fen Line services
stories.brief:
South West Norfolk MP Terry Jermy is urging the Transport Secretary to prioritise upgrades to Ely Junction. Following a summer that saw hundreds of cancellations on the Fen Line, Mr Jermy met with the Fen Line Users’ Association to discuss the impact on passengers in King’s Lynn, Downham Market, and Watlington. 

The MP highlighted issues including poor service reliability, cleanliness, and faulty air conditioning. While acknowledging that extreme weather has affected local peat soils, he argued that many delays remain avoidable. Mr Jermy is now pushing for the project to be included in the next government Spending Review to boost regional growth. Meanwhile, a new scheme launched on September 20 now allows passengers to use alternative operators if their train is cancelled.

stories.headline: Government consultation begins on Cambridgeshire local government changes
stories.brief:
A government consultation regarding the reorganisation of local government in Cambridgeshire is now underway. Residents are being invited to learn more about the proposed changes, specifically focusing on the details of option B. 

The consultation process is being highlighted by Cambridge City Council. Those living across the region can participate to understand how these potential structural adjustments might affect local administration. Further information on the specific proposals is available through official government channels.

stories.headline: Prison sentence for Cambridgeshire Crème Egg thief
stories.brief: A person has been jailed for stealing Crème Eggs. According to Cambridgeshire Constabulary, the individual was convicted following the theft of the confectionery items. No further details regarding the location or the specific circumstances of the incident have been released by the police at this time.

stories.headline: Peterborough Sports look to bounce back
stories.brief: Peterborough Sports are preparing for their next fixture following a recent defeat. The team is looking to recover quickly from the result, with players and staff focusing on an immediate opportunity to improve their performance. Supporters will be watching to see how the side responds in their upcoming match.

stories.headline: Proposals submitted for over 1,600 new homes in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: New plans have been unveiled that could see the construction of more than 1,600 homes in Cambridgeshire. According to reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, the proposed development has the potential to extend the footprint of the city. No further details regarding the specific location or timeline for the project have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: Historic Penny Farthing remains on display in March
stories.brief: A Penny Farthing bicycle has been a landmark feature above a garage in March for 115 years. The vintage cycle continues to be displayed at the site, marking over a century of local history.

stories.headline: World Grand Prix success for Luke Woodhouse
stories.brief: Darts player Luke Woodhouse has secured victory at the World Grand Prix. The professional darts player, who has connections to the local area, claimed the title following a successful performance in the tournament. The result was reported by Darts World Magazine.

stories.headline: Changes to waste collection in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Residents in East Cambridgeshire are seeing a change to how their household waste is collected. The local authority is moving away from the use of bags for rubbish, replacing them with wheelie bins. This update marks a new era for waste management services across the district. Householders are advised to look out for their new bins as the transition takes place.

stories.headline: New crematorium and bereavement centre opens in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Residents in East Cambridgeshire can now view the interior of the district’s newly completed crematorium and bereavement centre. The facility, which has recently been unveiled, is designed to provide local funeral services and support for the community. Further details regarding the site’s operations and services are expected to be available to the public as the centre begins its work.

stories.headline: Robbie Savage declines to comment on Peterborough United rumours
stories.brief: Former footballer Robbie Savage has refused to address ongoing speculation linking him to a managerial role at Peterborough United. Reports circulating in the sports media have suggested a potential connection between the broadcaster and the club, but Savage has remained tight-lipped regarding the claims. No official statement has been issued by Peterborough United concerning the vacancy or any prospective candidates.

stories.headline: Care Network Cambridgeshire marks 40th anniversary
stories.brief: Care Network Cambridgeshire is celebrating four decades of service to the local community. The organisation reached the milestone following a busy year, having provided support to 2,479 people throughout 2025.

stories.headline: Robbie Savage linked to Peterborough United role
stories.brief: Reports from The League Paper suggest that Robbie Savage could be set for a move into the English Football League with Peterborough United. The former professional footballer has been connected to a position at the club, though no further details regarding the nature of the potential role have been confirmed. Fans of the Posh will be watching closely to see if these links develop into a formal appointment in the coming weeks.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire crematorium evacuated shortly after opening
stories.brief: A newly opened crematorium in Cambridgeshire has been evacuated. The facility, which only began serving the public a few weeks ago, was cleared following an incident. No further details regarding the cause of the evacuation or the current status of the site have been provided.

stories.headline: Peterborough United dismiss managerial speculation
stories.brief: Peterborough United have officially denied reports regarding the club’s managerial position that circulated this past Sunday. Despite the club's statement, a prominent supporter has publicly suggested that Robbie Savage remains a genuine contender for the role. No further details regarding the club's leadership plans have been confirmed at this time.

stories.headline: Nine road closures announced across Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Motorists travelling across Cambridgeshire are being advised of nine upcoming road closures in the region. The Hunts Post reports that these disruptions are currently in place, and drivers are encouraged to check their routes before setting off. While specific locations and durations for the closures have not been detailed, residents are urged to stay informed about potential travel delays. Please plan your journeys accordingly to avoid any inconvenience while these works are carried out.

stories.headline: Peterborough Sports look to bounce back
stories.brief: Peterborough Sports are preparing for their next fixture following a recent defeat. The team is looking to recover quickly from the result, with players and staff focused on an immediate opportunity to improve their performance.

stories.headline: Smoke prompts evacuation at new crematorium during testing
stories.brief: A newly built crematorium has been evacuated following reports of increased smoke levels. The incident occurred while the facility was undergoing routine testing. No further details regarding the cause of the smoke or potential damage have been released at this time.

stories.headline: MP Stephen Barclay raises further questions regarding Saxon Pit
stories.brief: North East Cambridgeshire MP Stephen Barclay has submitted new questions concerning the Saxon Pit site in Whittlesey. The details of the inquiry follow recent reports regarding the location. No further information has been provided at this stage regarding the specific nature of the questions or the expected response from relevant authorities.

stories.headline: Evacuation at new crematorium following smoke during testing
stories.brief: A newly built crematorium has been evacuated after reports of increased smoke levels. The incident occurred while the facility was undergoing testing. No further details regarding the cause of the smoke or the current status of the site have been released.

stories.headline: Sutton extend lead in local derby
stories.brief: Sutton have moved 35 points clear at the top of the table following a decisive win in their latest derby match. The result, reported by the Spalding South Holland News, sees the side strengthen their position in the league standings.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire man convicted of attempted murder
stories.brief: A Cambridgeshire man has been convicted of attempting to kill his partner. The court heard that the defendant carried out a violent attack, which involved both stabbing the victim and attempting to electrocute her. The case was reported by the Hunts Post.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn man jailed for shoplifting
stories.brief:
A 39-year-old man from Gaywood has been sentenced to 12 weeks in prison after admitting to multiple thefts from a King’s Lynn supermarket. Shane Davis Wilson, of Pleasance Close, targeted the Heron Foods store in the town centre on three occasions in September. The court heard that he stole items including steak, wine, and sweets. 

Magistrates were told the defendant had breached a previous suspended sentence. In addition to the jail term, Davis Wilson has been ordered to pay £104.17 in compensation to the store. His defence solicitor stated that the thefts were committed due to financial difficulties and hunger.

stories.headline: High Sheriff commends Cambridgeshire hospice charity
stories.brief: The High Sheriff of Cambridgeshire has publicly praised a local hospice charity. In a recent statement, the High Sheriff highlighted the organisation for providing what was described as exceptional care. The commendation comes as the charity continues its work supporting patients and families across the region.

stories.headline: Heacham pupils join Shakespeare performances in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
Pupils from Heacham Junior School have taken part in the annual Robert Armin Festival at King’s Lynn Minster. Twenty-six Year 6 students attended the event to watch comedic adaptations of A Midsummer Night’s Dream and Romeo and Juliet, performed by 440 Theatre. 

During the productions, students and staff were invited to join the actors on stage. Assistant head teacher Ashley Kirwan participated in a scene from Romeo and Juliet, while teaching assistant Charlotte Guest also accompanied the group. Mr Kirwan noted that the festival’s humorous approach helps make Shakespeare’s work more accessible to young people, while strengthening their connection to the local history of the Elizabethan actor Robert Armin.

stories.headline: Bus routes cut in Cambridgeshire village despite new shelters
stories.brief: A Cambridgeshire village has seen its bus services cancelled, despite the recent installation of new shelters costing £16,000. The loss of these routes comes shortly after the investment was made to upgrade the local infrastructure. Residents are now facing a change to their public transport access following the decision to remove the services.

stories.headline: Speed checks carried out across Fenland
stories.brief: Police have conducted a day of action focused on road safety in the Fenland area. During the operation, officers monitored traffic and checked a total of 470 vehicles for speeding offences. The initiative was reported by the March Chatteris Whittlesey News.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn man fined after breaching town centre ban
stories.brief:
A prolific offender from King’s Lynn has been fined after failing to comply with a community protection notice. Twenty-nine-year-old Levi Coburn, of Anthony Nolan Road, appeared at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday. He admitted to breaching an order that bans him from entering the town centre.

The court heard that on September 2, Coburn refused to leave the town’s bus station when instructed by police. He shouted at officers while they were speaking with another individual. In mitigation, the court was told that Coburn was intoxicated at the time. He has been ordered to pay a total of £190, consisting of a £100 fine, a £40 victim surcharge, and £50 in court costs.

stories.headline: Peterborough teenager to join Kerry Ellis on tour
stories.brief: A 14-year-old from Peterborough is set to perform as part of Kerry Ellis’s upcoming Rock Anthems tour. The young musician will be joining the West End star on stage during the production. Further details regarding the specific dates or venues for the teenager's appearances have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Urgent search for missing man with Cambridgeshire links
stories.brief: Police have launched an urgent search for a man described as vulnerable who has known links to Cambridgeshire. Authorities are appealing for information to help locate him. Anyone who may have seen him or has information regarding his current whereabouts is urged to contact the police immediately.

stories.headline: Family pays tribute following fatal crash near Whittlesey
stories.brief: The family of a 21-year-old who died in a collision near Whittlesey have released a tribute. The individual was killed in a crash in the local area. No further details regarding the circumstances of the incident or the identity of the person involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Veterinary survey launched over potential dry eye food link
stories.brief: A new case survey has been launched following concerns regarding a potential link between certain pet foods and dry eye conditions. The investigation, reported by Vet Times, aims to gather data to better understand if specific dietary products are contributing to the health issue in animals. Pet owners are being encouraged to participate in the study to help clarify these concerns. Further information regarding the survey and its findings is expected to be released as the research progresses.

stories.headline: National award for Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service has been recognised with a national award. The organisation has been named a Menopause Friendly Employer. The accolade highlights the service's commitment to supporting staff members experiencing the menopause.

stories.headline: Police investigate violent assault in Spalding
stories.brief: Lincolnshire Police are investigating a violent incident in Spalding after a man was slashed during an altercation on a busy street. Reports indicate that the attack took place in a public area, with approximately twenty children witnessing the event. Authorities are currently looking into the circumstances surrounding the encounter. Anyone with information regarding the incident is encouraged to contact the local police force.

stories.headline: Emergency services called to new crematorium
stories.brief: A newly opened crematorium has been evacuated following an emergency response. Firefighters were called to the site just weeks after the facility first began operations. No further details regarding the cause of the incident or the current status of the building have been released at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Town FC hosts mental health talk with 8:56 Foundation
stories.brief:
King’s Lynn Town Football Club has hosted a mental health presentation for players and staff, delivered by the West Norfolk charity, the 8:56 Foundation. The session aimed to challenge the stigma surrounding mental health and encourage men to seek support rather than suffer in isolation.

Club media manager Conor Blake shared his personal experience of seeking help through the foundation, which provides free, funded talking therapy and peer support. The charity was established in memory of Lee Calton to promote open conversations about mental wellbeing. Linnets manager Paul Caddis described the presentation as a vital reminder that players and staff face the same human struggles as everyone else, emphasising the importance of looking out for one another.

stories.headline: Autumn events programme announced for King’s Lynn and West Norfolk
stories.brief:
A variety of cultural events are scheduled across King’s Lynn and West Norfolk this autumn. The King’s Lynn Festival has announced its new season, featuring coffee concerts and talks, while the West Norfolk Wyrdfest runs from October 8 to November 6 at various venues. 

Local museums are also hosting activities, with weekly lunchtime talks at True’s Yard and coffee mornings at Lynn Museum. Music fans can look forward to organ recitals at Lynn Minster, performances at the Hunstanton Bandstand, and a tribute to Whitney Houston. Additionally, the KLODS production of The Addams Family Musical takes place from October 29 to 31 at the Peter Hopkins Hall. Residents are encouraged to check venue websites for ticket availability and further information.

stories.headline: More human remains discovered at Peterborough roundabout
stories.brief: Archaeological work at a roundabout in Peterborough has revealed further human remains. The total number of skeletons recovered from the site has now reached 61. The discovery was reported by the BBC following ongoing investigations at the location.

stories.headline: Campaign group seeks to protect Cambridgeshire hospital services
stories.brief: A campaign group has pledged to ensure the voices of Cambridgeshire patients are heard regarding potential hospital service reductions. The group is responding to reports of possible cuts to local healthcare facilities. Further details on the specific hospitals affected or the nature of the proposed changes have not yet been confirmed. Residents are being encouraged to stay informed as the situation develops.

stories.headline: Nominations open for 2027 King’s Lynn and West Norfolk Mayor’s Business Awards
stories.brief:
Nominations are now open for the 38th annual Mayor’s Business Awards, which celebrate excellence across West Norfolk. Businesses are invited to put forward candidates for 11 categories, including the Apprentice and Trainee of the Year award, sponsored by Whitings Group. This specific category is open to individuals aged 35 or under who have demonstrated exceptional workplace contributions.

The awards ceremony will take place on Friday, March 5, 2027, at the Alive Corn Exchange in King’s Lynn. Organised by the Lynn News and Your Local Paper, the event highlights the achievements of the local business community. Interested parties have until 5pm on Friday, November 27, to submit their nominations. Further details are available through the event organisers.

stories.headline: Robbie Savage addresses Peterborough United manager speculation
stories.brief: Robbie Savage has commented on recent media reports suggesting he is a candidate for the vacant manager position at Peterborough United. The former footballer responded to claims linking him to the role at the club, following coverage published by the Peterborough Telegraph. No further details regarding the appointment process have been confirmed at this time.

stories.headline: Search continues for missing man with Cambridgeshire links
stories.brief: An urgent search is currently underway for a man who has reported links to the Cambridgeshire area. Authorities are continuing their efforts to locate him, though no further details regarding his identity or the circumstances of his disappearance have been released at this time. Residents are advised to keep an eye out for any official updates as the investigation proceeds.

stories.headline: Investigation launched after dog allegedly poisoned
stories.brief: An investigation is underway following reports that an emotional support dog has been poisoned. The owner of the animal has described feeling devastated by the incident. Further details regarding the location or the specific circumstances surrounding the event have not yet been released. Local residents are advised to remain vigilant while the matter is being looked into.

stories.headline: Fincham business seeks new charity partner
stories.brief:
The Farmhouse in Fincham is calling for nominations to find its next community charity partner for autumn 2026. The business is looking to support a local charity or not-for-profit group in West Norfolk with practical assistance, such as event promotion and venue space, rather than cash grants. 

Co-founder David Toulson-Burke says the initiative aims to highlight organisations making a difference in the region. Nominations are open to individuals and groups until October 10, with the successful partner to be announced later that month. Further details on how to submit a nomination can be found at thepigandpeacock.co.uk/community.

stories.headline: Peterborough United defeated in League One clash
stories.brief: Peterborough United have suffered a defeat in their latest League One fixture. The Posh were beaten one-nil away to Stockport County. Highlights of the match are now available via Sky Sports.

stories.headline: Irish success at Cambridgeshire horse race
stories.brief: A horse named Pierre Royal has secured a victory in Cambridgeshire. The win, which was reported by the East Cambridgeshire News, marks a successful outing for the Irish entry. No further details regarding the event or the specific race location have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Closure order issued for St Neots property
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Constabulary has confirmed that a closure order has been served on a residential property in St Neots. The legal action was carried out by local police officers. No further details regarding the address or the reasons behind the order have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Quarter-century milestone for King’s Lynn hospital radio presenter
stories.brief:
A long-serving presenter at Hospital Radio Lynn has marked 25 years of broadcasting. Mike Wing was joined by colleagues and former volunteers on Friday, September 18, to celebrate his quarter-century of service at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital. 

During his time at the station, Mr. Wing has served as a trustee and treasurer, and he currently hosts a weekly Friday afternoon programme. The show is well-known for its focus on 1960s music, a subject for which he has become a local authority. To mark the occasion, he was presented with a long-service certificate and received audio tributes from fellow broadcasters, including Hospital Broadcasting Association patron Alan Dedicoat.

stories.headline: Peterborough United defeated by Stockport County
stories.brief: Peterborough United have suffered a defeat in their latest League One fixture. The Posh were beaten 1-0 away at Stockport County.

stories.headline: Bus services to be cut in Cambridgeshire village
stories.brief: A Cambridgeshire village is set to lose all of its bus services. The news comes despite the community previously investing thousands of pounds into local bus shelters. The decision will impact residents who rely on public transport links in the area.

stories.headline: Road works and closures scheduled across Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Motorists in Cambridgeshire are being advised of upcoming disruption as road works and closures are planned across the county this week. Drivers are encouraged to plan their journeys in advance to account for potential delays caused by the maintenance. Local authorities have scheduled these works to take place throughout the coming days. Residents are reminded to check local travel updates before setting off to ensure they are aware of any specific routes affected in their area.

stories.headline: Police appeal for witnesses following King's Lynn upskirting incident
stories.brief:
Norfolk Police are appealing for information after an upskirting incident in King’s Lynn on Wednesday. At approximately 11:55am, a man reportedly took a photograph underneath a teenage girl’s skirt on Gaywood Road, between Archdale Street and Loke Road.

The suspect is described as a white man in his late 40s or early 50s, standing around 5ft 7ins tall with a large build, tanned skin, and no facial hair or tattoos. He was wearing a dark blue-grey sweater and dark trousers. Officers are asking anyone who witnessed the event or has relevant information to contact them via the police website or by calling 101, quoting crime reference number 36/72074/26.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire family tackle Holme Fen wildfire
stories.brief: A firefighting family from Cambridgeshire has worked together to tackle a major wildfire at Holme Fen. The crew members, who are related, were among those responding to the incident. No further details regarding the scale of the fire or the identities of those involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police investigate suspected arson near Fenland railway line
stories.brief: Authorities are treating a fire near railway tracks in the Fenland area as a case of arson. Emergency services were called to the scene following the blaze, which occurred in close proximity to the line. Police are now investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. Residents are advised that enquiries into the fire are ongoing.

stories.headline: New children’s roleplay centre opens in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
A new roleplay centre and café has opened in King’s Lynn town centre today. Located on Purfleet Street in the former Rusty Krab premises, Roleplay King’s Lynn features three age-specific zones for children up to the age of 15. Facilities include a soft play area for toddlers, a miniature town for younger children, and a gaming den for older siblings.

The business, established by a local family, also includes a café serving speciality drinks and homemade snacks. The centre is open seven days a week, offering three 90-minute sessions daily. The team is also inviting schools and support groups to arrange exclusive bookings to provide a welcoming environment for children with special educational needs and disabilities.

stories.headline: Seven-year-old boy dies following incident in Wimblington
stories.brief: A seven-year-old boy has died following reports of a child in the water at Wimblington. Emergency services were called to the scene, but the child could not be saved. No further details regarding the circumstances of the incident have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Tributes paid to former Queen Elizabeth Hospital surgeon Graham Thompson
stories.brief: Tributes have been paid to Graham Thompson, a former surgeon at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn, who has died at the age of 96. Mr Thompson, who passed away on Wednesday, September 9, began his career in the Royal Navy before working in Wisbech and later moving to the QEH. He retired in 1994 but remained active in the medical community, establishing a walking group for retired consultants. His family described him as a remarkable man who transformed many lives during his career. A funeral service will be held at the West Suffolk Crematorium in Risby on Wednesday, October 7, at 12.30pm.

stories.headline: Death of Phoebe Bird from Long Sutton
stories.brief: The death of Phoebe Bird has been announced. According to an obituary published in the Lincolnshire Free Press, the resident of Long Sutton passed away in 2022. No further details regarding the circumstances of her death or funeral arrangements have been provided.

stories.headline: Teacher to face three-day misconduct hearing
stories.brief: A teacher is due to appear before a three-day misconduct hearing. The details of the case were reported by The Hunts Post. No further information regarding the identity of the individual or the nature of the allegations has been released at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn to host annual steampunk celebration
stories.brief:
King’s Lynn Steampunk Society is hosting a day of themed entertainment on Saturday, October 3. The event begins with a free bazaar at St Nicholas’ Chapel, running from 10am until 4pm. Visitors can browse stalls featuring crafts, clothing, and jewellery, while enjoying live music and a hat competition. Author Tracee Findlater will also launch her latest book during the day.

The celebrations conclude with a 6pm screening of the film Chitty Chitty Bang Bang at the Majestic Cinema. Organised alongside the Lynn Community Cinema Club, the screening encourages audience participation and fancy dress. Tickets for the film are available through the Majestic Cinema website or at the box office.

stories.headline: Fire reported at household recycling centre
stories.brief: A fire has broken out at a household recycling centre. Emergency services were called to the scene to deal with the blaze. No further details regarding the location or the impact on local services have been provided at this time. Residents are advised to monitor local updates for any potential disruption to waste disposal facilities in the area.

stories.headline: Care home staff in Long Sutton and Spalding receive awards
stories.brief: Staff working at care homes in Long Sutton and Spalding have been formally recognised for their service. According to reports from the Spalding South Holland News, employees at the facilities were presented with awards for their ongoing work. No further details regarding the specific nature of the recognition or the individuals involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Man arrested following drugs stop in the Fens
stories.brief: Police have arrested a man in the Fens following a stop related to illegal drugs. Authorities confirmed that the individual is currently subject to a ban preventing him from entering the United Kingdom. No further details regarding the location of the stop or the specific charges have been released at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn man fined following Tower Gardens incident
stories.brief:
A 38-year-old man has been fined after refusing to leave Tower Gardens in King’s Lynn. On July 3, police encountered Aleksandr Los, of Guanock Place, surrounded by beer cans and unable to stand properly. Officers reported that Mr Los refused to engage with them and shouted and swore in Romanian. 

He was subsequently arrested for being drunk and disorderly. During a hearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Mr Los pleaded guilty to the charge. He told the court that he has since stopped drinking. The bench ordered him to pay a total of £271, consisting of a £133 fine, a £53 victim surcharge, and £85 in court costs.

stories.headline: Firefighters attend shed blaze in Spalding
stories.brief: Fire crews have been called to tackle a shed fire in the Spalding area. According to reports from the Spalding South Holland News, emergency services attended the scene to deal with the incident. No further details regarding the cause of the fire or any potential injuries have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over Queen Elizabeth Hospital services and new build delays
stories.brief:
North West Norfolk MP James Wild has criticised the recent Queen Elizabeth Hospital Annual Members’ Meeting, describing it as a missed opportunity to reassure the public. Mr Wild stated that officials failed to guarantee the future of key services, including A&E, ICU, and maternity care, amid ongoing discussions regarding a clinical strategy review.

The meeting also revealed that the completion date for the new hospital has been pushed back to 2033. Mr Wild has written to the Health Secretary to urge that the previously promised 2032 deadline be maintained. Proposals for the clinical review are expected to go before the group board at the end of October, with a scrutiny session by Norfolk County Council scheduled for November.

stories.headline: Peterborough MP establishes connection with Canadian namesake
stories.brief: The Member of Parliament for Peterborough has formed new links with a constituency of the same name in Canada. The connection was reported by the Peterborough Telegraph. No further details regarding the nature of the partnership or any planned joint initiatives have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Evacuation at new crematorium following testing
stories.brief: A newly built crematorium has been evacuated after staff reported an increased level of smoke during testing procedures. The incident occurred at the site as officials carried out initial checks on the facility's equipment. No further details regarding the cause of the smoke or potential damage have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Fire causes severe damage to Long Sutton park bench
stories.brief: A park bench in Long Sutton has been left severely damaged following a fire. The incident was reported by LincsOnline, noting the extent of the destruction caused to the public seating area. No further details regarding the cause of the blaze or any potential witnesses have been released at this time. Residents are advised that the bench is currently out of use due to the damage sustained.

stories.headline: Emergency services attend collision in Fenland town
stories.brief: Emergency crews have been called to the scene of a road traffic collision involving a car and a pedestrian. The incident occurred in a Fenland town, according to reports from the Cambs Times. No further details regarding the exact location or the condition of those involved have been released at this time. Motorists are advised to remain aware of potential disruption in the area while emergency teams carry out their work.

stories.headline: Tilney St Lawrence man disqualified for drink-driving in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
A man from Tilney St Lawrence has been banned from the roads after being caught drink-driving at a King’s Lynn retail park. Tom Perry, of St Johns Road, was stopped by police at Hardwick Retail Park on September 4 following reports of antisocial behaviour in the area. 

Officers conducted a breath test which showed Perry had 73 micrograms of alcohol in 100 millilitres of breath, more than double the legal limit of 35. Appearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Perry pleaded guilty to the offence. He has been disqualified from driving for 16 months and ordered to pay a total of £812 in fines and costs.

stories.headline: Peterborough business group marks centenary
stories.brief: A major business organisation in Peterborough has celebrated its one-hundredth anniversary. More than 400 guests attended the event to mark the group's centenary milestone.

stories.headline: Care home in March rated as failing to provide good standard of care
stories.brief: A care home in March has been criticised for its performance. According to a report from the Cambs Times, the facility failed to provide a good standard of care for its residents. No further details regarding the specific nature of the failings or the name of the home have been provided at this time.
